Explained in [Types: Integers](language-types.md#integers).

| Name | Declaration | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `u8` | `type u8 = bigint`<br>`function u8(value: bigint): u8` | Unsigned 8-bit integer (a `bigint` to TypeScript); literals are written `1n`. |
| `u16` | `type u16 = bigint`<br>`function u16(value: bigint): u16` | Unsigned 16-bit integer (a `bigint` to TypeScript); literals are written `1n`. |
| `u32` | `type u32 = bigint`<br>`function u32(value: bigint): u32` | Unsigned 32-bit integer (a `bigint` to TypeScript); literals are written `1n`. |
| `u64` | `type u64 = bigint`<br>`function u64(value: bigint): u64` | Unsigned 64-bit integer (a `bigint` to TypeScript); literals are written `1n`. |
| `u128` | `type u128 = bigint`<br>`function u128(value: bigint): u128` | Unsigned 128-bit integer (a `bigint` to TypeScript); literals are written `1n`. |
| `u256` | `type u256 = bigint`<br>`function u256(value: bigint): u256` | 256-bit unsigned integers for computation (sqrt-price and liquidity math): locals, helper parameters and results, `u256(x)` and back with `u128(x)` / `u64(x)` (checked). |
| `i8` | `type i8 = bigint`<br>`function i8(value: bigint): i8` | Signed 8-bit integer, two's complement (a `bigint` to TypeScript). |
| `i16` | `type i16 = bigint`<br>`function i16(value: bigint): i16` | Signed 16-bit integer, two's complement (a `bigint` to TypeScript). |
| `i32` | `type i32 = bigint`<br>`function i32(value: bigint): i32` | Signed 32-bit integer, two's complement (a `bigint` to TypeScript). |
| `i64` | `type i64 = bigint`<br>`function i64(value: bigint): i64` | Signed 64-bit integer, two's complement (a `bigint` to TypeScript). |
| `i128` | `type i128 = bigint`<br>`function i128(value: bigint): i128` | Signed 128-bit integer, two's complement (a `bigint` to TypeScript). |
| `mulDiv` | `function mulDiv(a: u64, b: u64, c: u64): u64` | floor(a * b / c) with a double-width intermediate (all u64, all u128, or all u256); aborts if c is 0 or the result does not fit. |
| `mulDivCeil` | `function mulDivCeil(a: u64, b: u64, c: u64): u64` | ceil(a * b / c), like mulDiv. |
| `isqrt` | `function isqrt<T>(x: T): T` | floor(sqrt(x)) for unsigned integers (u8 … u256). |
| `min` | `function min<T>(a: T, b: T): T` | The smaller of two integers of one type. |
| `max` | `function max<T>(a: T, b: T): T` | The larger of two integers of one type. |
| `f64` | `type f64 = bigint & { readonly __f64: unique symbol }` | A 64-bit float, held as its IEEE 754 bits (Borsh writes an f64 as those 8 bytes, little-endian); the IDL calls it f64. |
| `f64FromBits` | `function f64FromBits(bits: u64): f64` | An f64 from its IEEE 754 bits, computed with integers. |
| `f64Bits` | `function f64Bits(value: f64): u64` | An f64's IEEE 754 bits. |

## Account types

Explained in [Accounts: Account parameters and the checks they emit](language-accounts.md#account-parameters-and-the-checks-they-emit).

| Name | Declaration | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AccountMeta` | `interface AccountMeta` | Fields every account parameter exposes. |
| `Signer` | `interface Signer` | The account must have signed the transaction. |
| `SystemAccount` | `interface SystemAccount` | An account owned by the System Program, e.g. a wallet (Anchor `SystemAccount`; 3011 otherwise). |
| `AccountInfo` | `interface AccountInfo` | Any account, no ownership or data checks. |
| `Account` | `type Account<T> = Readonly<T> & AccountMeta` | An account owned by this program holding struct `T`. |
| `Mut` | `type Mut<T, E> = T & AccountMeta` | A writable account: `Mut<T>` is `Account<T>` whose fields may be written. |
| `Init` | `type Init<T>` | An account this instruction creates: at a PDA of this program, or, with `null` seeds, a new keypair account that signs. |
| `InitIfNeeded` | `type InitIfNeeded<T>` | Created on first use (like Anchor `init_if_needed`): `createIfNeeded(payer, seeds)` returns true when it created the account now. |
| `Zeroed` | `type Zeroed<T> = T & AccountMeta` | An account the client already allocated with System CreateAccount (any size up to 10 MiB; over 10 KiB a program cannot create it itself), owned by this program and still zeroed: Anchor's `zero`. |
| `Migrate` | `interface Migrate<From, To>` | Anchor 1.0's `Migration<From, To>`: an existing `From` account (owner, discriminator and size checked) that this instruction rewrites as `To` with `acct.migrate(payer, value)`, a top-level statement every path must reach. |
| `Dup` | `type Dup<A> = A & { readonly __dup?: true }` | Anchor's `dup`: this writable account may be the same account as another writable parameter (TypeSOL refuses that otherwise, 2040). |
| `Optional` | `type Optional<A> = A \| null` | An optional account (Anchor `Option<Account<…>>`): the client passes this program's id in its slot to leave it out. |
| `ProgramData` | `interface ProgramData` | This program's ProgramData account (BPF upgradeable loader). |
| `Program` | `interface Program<Address>` | Another program, pinned to its address: `Program<"Tokenz...">`. |
| `UncheckedProgram` | `interface UncheckedProgram` | Any executable account. |
| `SystemProgram` | `interface SystemProgram` | The System Program. |
| `EventAuthority` | `interface EventAuthority` | Anchor's event authority PDA ["__event_authority"] of this program (address checked), for emitCpi. |
| `SelfProgram` | `interface SelfProgram` | This program itself (its address is checked), for self-CPI. |

## Constraints

Explained in [Accounts: Constraints](language-accounts.md#constraints).

| Name | Declaration | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HasOne` | `type HasOne<A, Field, E> = A & { readonly __hasOne?: [Field, E] }` | `HasOne<A, "field">`: the struct's `field` must be the key of the parameter with that name (Anchor's `has_one`; 2001). |
| `Seeds` | `type Seeds<A, Names, Bump, ProgramId>` | The account is this program's PDA for the seeds (Anchor's `seeds = […], bump`; 2006): `"@name"` is an account's key or an argument's bytes, `"@acct.field"` a field, other strings literals. |
| `CloseTo` | `type CloseTo<A, Destination> = A & { readonly __closeTo?: Destination }` | Close the account into the parameter `Destination` when the instruction succeeds (Anchor's `close = destination`). |
| `Address` | `type Address<A, Base58, E> = A & { readonly __address?: [Base58, E] }` | The account must be this exact address (Anchor `address = …`, error 2012): `Address<Mut<AccountInfo>, "4Nd1…">`. |
| `Owner` | `type Owner<A, Base58, E> = A & { readonly __owner?: [Base58, E] }` | The account's owner program must be this address (Anchor `owner = …`, 2004; a third argument: one of your errors). |
| `Executable` | `type Executable<A> = A & { readonly __executable?: true }` | The account must be an executable program (Anchor `executable`, 2007). |
| `Signed` | `type Signed<A, E> = A & { readonly __signed?: E \| true }` | The account must sign the transaction (Anchor's `signer` constraint on an account that is not a `Signer`; 2002), e.g. `Signed<Zeroed<Multisig>>` for an account the client creates with a fresh keypair in the same transaction. |
| `constraint` | `function constraint(account: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount \| null, condition: boolean, error?: string \| AnchorError): void` | Anchor's `constraint = condition @ error` on `account`. |

## Closing and resizing

Explained in [Accounts: Closing and resizing](language-accounts.md#closing-and-resizing).

| Name | Declaration | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `close` | `function close(account: AccountMeta, destination: AccountMeta): void` | Close a program-owned account: move all lamports to `destination` and wipe it. |
| `realloc` | `function realloc(account: AccountMeta, newSize: u64, payer: Mut<Signer>): void` | Resize an account of this program (Anchor `realloc`, struct accounts only): growing charges `payer` the extra rent (never the account's own lamports, which may be deposits); shrinking keeps every lamport in the account — move freed rent out yourself if your program allows it. |
| `resizeAccount` | `function resizeAccount(account: RemainingAccount \| Mut<AccountInfo>, newSize: u64): void` | Resize a `Mut<AccountInfo>` or a remaining account of this program to `newSize` bytes (Rust's `AccountInfo::resize` / `realloc(newSize, true)`): the data length only, the new bytes zeroed. |

## Remaining accounts and other programs' accounts

Explained in [Accounts: Remaining accounts](language-accounts.md#remaining-accounts).

| Name | Declaration | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `remainingAccounts` | `function remainingAccounts(): RemainingAccounts` | The accounts passed after the declared ones, in order (see RemainingAccounts). |
| `RemainingAccount` | `interface RemainingAccount` | One extra account passed after the declared ones. |
| `RemainingAccounts` | `interface RemainingAccounts` | The accounts a client passed beyond the instruction's declared parameters. |
| `RemainingSlice` | `interface RemainingSlice` | Part of the remaining accounts (`rest.slice(a, b)`): spread it into a CPI's account list, directly or via readonly/writable. |
| `loadAccount` | `function loadAccount<T>(account: RemainingAccount \| AccountInfo): Account<T>` | Read a struct of this program from a remaining account or an `AccountInfo` parameter (Anchor's `AccountLoader::try_from` on an `UncheckedAccount`): owner, discriminator and size are checked. |
| `loadAccountMut` | `function loadAccountMut<T>(account: RemainingAccount \| AccountInfo): Mut<T>` | `loadAccount` for writing: also writable, and loaded mutably once per instruction (2040). |
| `loadForeign` | `function loadForeign<T>(account: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount, owner: Pubkey): Readonly<T>` | View another program's Anchor account as a struct declared here (same field layout): the owner must be `owner` (3007), the data must start with the discriminator sha256("account:<T>")[..8] (3002) and be large enough (3003). |
| `readData` | `function readData<T>(account: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount, offset: u64): T` | Read a little-endian value at `offset` in any account's data (bounds-checked, error 3003): `readData<u64>(pool, 72n)`, `readData<Pubkey>(pool, 8n)`. |
| `writeData` | `function writeData<T>(account: Mut<AccountInfo>, offset: u64, value: T): void` | Write a little-endian value at `offset` in a `Mut<AccountInfo>`'s data (bounds-checked, error 3003): `writeData<u64>(archive, 72n, count)`. |

## PDAs

Explained in [PDAs](language-pdas.md).

| Name | Declaration | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Seed` | `type Seed = string \| Pubkey \| Hash \| bigint \| number` | A PDA seed: a string, a Pubkey, a Hash (its 32 bytes), an integer (at its width) or a unit enum value (one byte). |
| `SignerSeeds` | `interface SignerSeeds` | The seeds (with the bump) of one PDA signature, for helpers that sign CPIs: declare a `seeds: SignerSeeds` parameter, pass it where signerSeeds go, and call the helper with `signer(["vault", owner.key, bump])` (or `signer([])` when nothing needs to sign). |
| `signer` | `function signer(seeds: Seed[]): SignerSeeds` | Name one PDA signature's seeds (with the bump) for CPIs and helpers: `const vault = signer(["vault", owner.key, bump])`. |
| `requirePda` | `function requirePda(account: AccountMeta, seeds: Seed[], bump: u8): void` | Verify `account.key` is the PDA for `seeds` + `bump` under this program. |
| `bigEndian` | `function bigEndian(value: bigint): Seed` | An integer seed with its bytes most significant first (Rust's `x.to_be_bytes()`), inside a seeds list: `["tick_array", pool.key, bigEndian(startIndex)]`. |
| `findProgramAddress` | `function findProgramAddress(seeds: Seed[], program: Pubkey): Pubkey` | The canonical program address of `seeds` under `program` (Rust `Pubkey::find_program_address(seeds, program).0`). |
| `findProgramAddressBump` | `function findProgramAddressBump(seeds: Seed[], program: Pubkey): u8` | The bump of that canonical program address (`Pubkey::find_program_address(seeds, program).1`), to sign with it. |
| `findProgramAddressWithBump` | `function findProgramAddressWithBump(seeds: Seed[], program: Pubkey): [address: Pubkey, bump: u8]` | The canonical program address and its bump from one search (Rust's `let (address, bump) = Pubkey::find_program_address(seeds, program)`), where `findProgramAddress` and `findProgramAddressBump` would search twice: bind both, `const [address, bump] = findProgramAddressWithBump(["seat", market, trader], PHOENIX_ID)`. |
| `createProgramAddress` | `function createProgramAddress(seeds: Seed[], program: Pubkey): Pubkey \| null` | `Pubkey::create_program_address(seeds, program)`: the address of these seeds with the bump given as the last seed, or null when they give no program address (a point on the curve, or too many / too long seeds). |
| `programId` | `function programId(): Pubkey` | This program's address (`crate::ID`). |

## Calling other programs

Explained in [Calling other programs: invoke](language-cpi.md#invoke).

| Name | Declaration | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invoke` | `function invoke(program: Program<string> \| UncheckedProgram \| SystemProgram \| TokenProgram \| Token2022Program \| TokenInterface \| RemainingAccount, accounts: CpiAccount[], data: CpiData[], signerSeeds?: Seed[] \| SignerSeeds \| (Seed[] \| SignerSeeds)[]): void` | Call any program (a cross-program invocation) with an account list and instruction data. |
| `CpiAccount` | `interface CpiAccount` | An account entry for `invoke`, built with readonly()/writable()/readonlySigner()/writableSigner(). |
| `readonly` | `function readonly(account: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount \| null): CpiAccount`<br>`function readonly(accounts: RemainingAccounts \| RemainingSlice): Iterable<CpiAccount>` | A read-only entry of `invoke`'s account list: an account, or remaining accounts spread (`...readonly(rest)`). |
| `writable` | `function writable(account: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount \| null): CpiAccount`<br>`function writable(accounts: RemainingAccounts \| RemainingSlice): Iterable<CpiAccount>` | A writable account entry for `invoke` (the parameter must be `Mut<…>`); an optional account as for `readonly`. |
| `readonlySigner` | `function readonlySigner(account: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount): CpiAccount` | A read-only signer entry for `invoke`: the account signed, or signerSeeds sign for it. |
| `writableSigner` | `function writableSigner(account: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount): CpiAccount` | A writable signer entry for `invoke`: the account signed, or signerSeeds sign for it. |
| `CpiData` | `type CpiData` | Instruction data pieces, Borsh-encoded: integers little-endian at their declared width, booleans 1 byte, Pubkeys/Hashes 32 bytes, strings u32 length + UTF-8, Options a tag byte + value, structs and FixedArrays their fixed layout, unit enum values 1 byte, data enums as Borsh enums, Vec arguments u32 length + elements. |
| `Bytes` | `interface Bytes` | Raw bytes for instruction data. |
| `sighash` | `function sighash(name: string): Bytes` | The 8-byte Anchor instruction discriminator for `name` (sha256("global:<snake_case name>")[..8]). |
| `hex` | `function hex(literal: string): Bytes` | Bytes from a hex string literal, e.g. hex("0a0b"). |
| `returnData` | `function returnData<T>(program: AccountMeta): T` | Read the return data the last invoke() left behind, checking it came from `program` and has exactly the size of T: `const n = returnData<u64>(counterProgram)`. |
| `invokeInstruction` | `function invokeInstruction(programId: Pubkey, accounts: IndexedList<InstructionAccountMeta>, data: IndexedList<u8>, infos: RemainingAccounts \| RemainingSlice, signerSeeds?: Seed[] \| SignerSeeds \| (Seed[] \| SignerSeeds)[]): void` | A CPI decided at run time, e.g. one stored in account data (Rust's `invoke_signed(&Instruction { program_id, accounts, data }, infos, seeds)`). |
| `InstructionAccountMeta` | `interface InstructionAccountMeta` | One account of an instruction built at run time (Rust's `AccountMeta`): any struct with these three fields. |
| `programAt` | `function programAt<P>(account: RemainingAccount \| AccountInfo): P` | A remaining account (or an AccountInfo parameter) as a typed program: `const stake = programAt<StakeProgram>(rest.get(12n))`, then `stake.split(…)`, `token.mintTo(…)`, `system.transfer(…)` as on a declared program parameter, and passed to helpers that take that program type. |
| `sysvarAt` | `function sysvarAt<S>(account: RemainingAccount \| AccountInfo): S` | A remaining account (or an AccountInfo parameter) as a sysvar read in place: `sysvarAt<StakeHistorySysvar>(acct)`, bound to a const, then `.count`, `.latestEpoch`, `.effective(epoch)` …. |
| `named` | `function named(account: AccountMeta, address: Pubkey): NamedAccount` | A Stake CPI's sysvar or stake config argument as solana_program's stake instruction builders write it: the instruction's account list names `address` (`SysvarC1ock…`), and `account` (the slot's account, whatever its key) is the account handed to the runtime, as Rust's `invoke_signed(&ix, &[stake, clock_info, …])` hands it. |
| `NamedAccount` | `interface NamedAccount` | An account whose slot in a Stake CPI names another address: what `named(account, address)` gives. |

| --- | --- | --- |
| `transferFee` | `function transferFee(mint: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount, amount: u64): u64` | The fee withheld when `amount` is sent now: the mint's Token-2022 TransferFeeConfig for the current epoch, 0 without it. |
| `transferFeeInverse` | `function transferFeeInverse(mint: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount, amountReceived: u64): u64` | The fee withheld when the recipient is to get `amountReceived` (spl-token-2022's `calculate_inverse_epoch_fee`): send `amountReceived + transferFeeInverse(mint, amountReceived)`. 0 without TransferFeeConfig; fails (5100) where spl-token-2022 has no answer. |
| `transferFeeBasisPoints` | `function transferFeeBasisPoints(mint: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount): u16` | The TransferFeeConfig in force this epoch: its basis points (0 without the extension). |
| `transferFeeMaximum` | `function transferFeeMaximum(mint: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount): u64` | The TransferFeeConfig in force this epoch: its maximum fee (0 without the extension). |
| `extensionsWithin` | `function extensionsWithin(account: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount, types: u16[]): boolean` | Whether every Token-2022 extension of `account` is one of `types` (a list of u16 extension types, e.g. `[1n, 18n, 19n, 10n, 25n]`): a pool that accepts only mints it knows how to handle. |
| `hasExtension` | `function hasExtension(account: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount, extensionType: u16): boolean` | Whether a Token-2022 mint or token account carries extension `extensionType` (e.g. 9 NonTransferable, 7 ImmutableOwner). |
| `transferHookProgram` | `function transferHookProgram(mint: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount): Option<Pubkey>` | The TransferHook extension's program, if any. |
| `transferHookAuthority` | `function transferHookAuthority(mint: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount): Option<Pubkey>` | The TransferHook extension's authority (who may change the hook program), if any. |
| `permanentDelegate` | `function permanentDelegate(mint: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount): Option<Pubkey>` | The PermanentDelegate extension's delegate, if any (it can move or burn anyone's tokens). |
| `mintCloseAuthority` | `function mintCloseAuthority(mint: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount): Option<Pubkey>` | The MintCloseAuthority extension's authority, if any. |
| `isTransferring` | `function isTransferring(tokenAccount: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount): boolean` | Whether Token-2022 is transferring from this token account right now (its TransferHookAccount `transferring` flag): true inside a transfer hook called by Token-2022, false when the hook is invoked directly. |

## Transfer hooks

Explained in [Calling other programs: Implementing another program's interface (transfer hooks)](language-cpi.md#implementing-another-programs-interface-transfer-hooks).

| Name | Declaration | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `initExtraAccountMetas` | `function initExtraAccountMetas(payer: Mut<Signer>, account: AccountMeta, mint: AccountMeta, systemProgram: SystemProgram, extraAccounts?: ExtraAccountMeta[]): void` | Create the transfer-hook validation account (an ExtraAccountMetaList) at PDA ["extra-account-metas", mint], listing the extra accounts Token-2022 passes to the hook after the standard four and this account (so the first extra account has index 5). |
| `updateExtraAccountMetas` | `function updateExtraAccountMetas(payer: Mut<Signer>, account: AccountMeta, mint: AccountMeta, systemProgram: SystemProgram, extraAccounts?: ExtraAccountMeta[]): void` | Rewrite this program's existing ExtraAccountMetaList for `mint` (Rust `ExtraAccountMetaList::update`), resizing it to the new list; `payer` tops it up to the rent of the new size when needed. |
| `ExtraAccountMeta` | `type ExtraAccountMeta` | One extra account of a transfer hook's ExtraAccountMetaList: a fixed address, or a PDA from seeds (see initExtraAccountMetas). |
| `ExtraAccountSeed` | `interface ExtraAccountSeed` | A seed of an extra account resolved by Token-2022 at transfer time (seedAccountKey, seedAccountData, seedInstructionData). |
| `seedAccountKey` | `function seedAccountKey(index: bigint): ExtraAccountSeed` | Seed::AccountKey: the key of the account at this index of the execute instruction. |
| `seedAccountData` | `function seedAccountData(index: bigint, offset: bigint, length: bigint): ExtraAccountSeed` | Seed::AccountData: `length` bytes at `offset` of the data of the account at `index`. |
| `seedInstructionData` | `function seedInstructionData(offset: bigint, length: bigint): ExtraAccountSeed` | Seed::InstructionData: `length` bytes at `offset` of the execute instruction's data. |

| `CorePlugin` | `type CorePlugin` | A Metaplex Core plugin, written as an object literal (Core's Plugin enum, with its authority when it is added). |
| `CorePluginKind` | `type CorePluginKind = CorePlugin["kind"] \| "Groups"` | The name of a Metaplex Core plugin, as `removePlugin` and the plugin readers take it. |
| `CorePluginAuthority` | `type CorePluginAuthority = "none" \| "owner" \| "updateAuthority" \| Pubkey` | Who manages a Metaplex Core plugin: `"owner"`, `"updateAuthority"`, `"none"` (nobody: fixed), or an address. |
| `CoreExternalPlugin` | `type CoreExternalPlugin` | A Metaplex Core external plugin adapter, written as an object literal: data a third party writes (`AppData`), an account that approves or rejects lifecycle events (`Oracle`), or a program called on them (`LifecycleHook`); the `Linked` forms go on a collection, for each of its assets. |
| `CoreExternalPluginKey` | `type CoreExternalPluginKey` | Which external plugin: an AppData by its data authority, an Oracle by its base address, a LifecycleHook by its program. |
| `CoreLifecycleCheck` | `interface CoreLifecycleCheck` | When a Core lifecycle event reaches an external plugin, and what the plugin may do about it. |
| `CoreExtraAccount` | `type CoreExtraAccount` | An account Core passes to an external plugin: one it already has, or an address. |

## Sysvars

Explained in [Sysvars, hashes, signatures and oracles: Sysvars](language-chain.md#sysvars).

| Name | Declaration | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `now` | `function now(): i64` | Current cluster unix timestamp (Clock sysvar). |
| `currentSlot` | `function currentSlot(): u64` | The current slot (Clock sysvar). |
| `currentEpoch` | `function currentEpoch(): u64` | The current epoch (Clock sysvar). |
| `epochStartTimestamp` | `function epochStartTimestamp(): i64` | The Unix time the current epoch started at (Clock.epoch_start_timestamp). |
| `slotsPerEpoch` | `function slotsPerEpoch(): u64` | The number of slots in an epoch after warmup (EpochSchedule sysvar). |
| `epochWarmup` | `function epochWarmup(): boolean` | Whether epochs warm up (EpochSchedule sysvar). |
| `firstNormalEpoch` | `function firstNormalEpoch(): u64` | The first epoch after warmup (EpochSchedule sysvar). |
| `firstNormalSlot` | `function firstNormalSlot(): u64` | The first slot after warmup (EpochSchedule sysvar). |
| `lastRestartSlot` | `function lastRestartSlot(): u64` | The LastRestartSlot sysvar: the last slot the cluster restarted at (0 if never). |
| `epochRewards` | `function epochRewards(): EpochRewards` | The EpochRewards sysvar through the `sol_get_epoch_rewards_sysvar` syscall, Rust's `EpochRewards::get()` (no account needed). |
| `EpochRewards` | `interface EpochRewards` | The EpochRewards sysvar, as `epochRewards()` reads it: read-only; keep it in a local (`const er = epochRewards()`). |
| `minimumBalance` | `function minimumBalance(account: AccountMeta): u64` | Rent-exempt minimum for `account`'s current data length. |
| `SlotHashesSysvar` | `interface SlotHashesSysvar` | The SlotHashes sysvar (`SysvarS1otHashes…`), read as an account: it is too large for the sysvar syscalls (Anchor's `Sysvar<SlotHashes>` cannot load it either). |
| `StakeHistorySysvar` | `interface StakeHistorySysvar` | The StakeHistory sysvar (`SysvarStakeHistory…`), read as an account: the cluster's stake per recent epoch (up to 512, newest first), as the Stake program uses it for warmup and cooldown. |
| `stackHeight` | `function stackHeight(): u64` | How deep in cross-program calls this program runs: 1 when the transaction calls it directly, more when another program invoked it. |
| `processedSiblingInstructionCount` | `function processedSiblingInstructionCount(): u64` | How many instructions the caller of this program has already invoked at this program's stack height (its processed siblings), or, when the transaction calls this program directly, how many top-level instructions ran before this one (Rust's `get_processed_sibling_instruction(i)` until it returns None). |
| `processedSiblingInstruction` | `function processedSiblingInstruction(index: u64): TransactionInstruction` | Processed sibling instruction `index` (0 the latest), as Rust's `get_processed_sibling_instruction(index)` reads it with the `sol_get_processed_sibling_instruction` syscall: its program id, accounts and data, as a TransactionInstruction. 5104 when there is none at that index. |

## Hashes, signatures and introspection

Explained in [Sysvars, hashes, signatures and oracles: Hashing](language-chain.md#hashing).

| Name | Declaration | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sha256` | `function sha256(...parts: (string \| Pubkey \| Hash \| bigint \| boolean)[]): Hash` | sha256 over the parts concatenated: strings (UTF-8), Pubkeys/Hashes (32 bytes), integers (LE), booleans (1 byte). |
| `keccak256` | `function keccak256(...parts: (string \| Pubkey \| Hash \| bigint \| boolean)[]): Hash` | keccak256 over the parts concatenated, encoded as for sha256. |
| `merkleVerify` | `function merkleVerify(leaf: Hash, proof: Vec<Hash>, root: Hash): boolean` | Whether `proof` places `leaf` under `root` (keccak256, sorted pairs: the OpenZeppelin convention most airdrop tools use). |
| `verifyEd25519` | `function verifyEd25519(instructions: InstructionsSysvar, signer: Pubkey, message: string \| Hash \| Pubkey): boolean` | Whether this transaction contains an Ed25519 precompile instruction that verified `message` signed by `signer` (offsets inside the precompile's own data). |
| `verifySecp256k1` | `function verifySecp256k1(hash: Hash, recoveryId: u8, r: Hash, s: Hash, ethAddress: Hash): boolean` | Whether the secp256k1 signer of `hash`, recovered from (r, s, recoveryId), is an Ethereum address given left-padded to 32 bytes (12 zero bytes + 20 address bytes). |
| `ethMessageHash` | `function ethMessageHash(message: string): Hash` | The hash an Ethereum wallet signs for `personal_sign` (EIP-191): keccak256("\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\n" + length + message). |
| `InstructionsSysvar` | `interface InstructionsSysvar` | The Instructions sysvar (Sysvar1nstructions…): every instruction of the transaction being executed. |
| `TransactionInstruction` | `interface TransactionInstruction` | One instruction of the transaction, read from the Instructions sysvar. |

| Name | Declaration | What it is |

| `pythPrice` | `function pythPrice(update: PythPriceUpdate, feedId: Hash, maxAgeSeconds: u64, exponent?: i32): i64` | Like Pyth's get_price_no_older_than: fully verified, `feedId` matches, published within `maxAgeSeconds` (5111 otherwise). |

## Native programs

Explained in [Porting a native program (advanced)](language-native.md).

| Name | Declaration | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `instructionData` | `function instructionData(): InstructionBytes` | The instruction data as sent, discriminator included: `const data = instructionData()`, then `data.length`, `data.get(i)`, or pass it on to `invokeInstruction`. |
| `InstructionBytes` | `interface InstructionBytes` | The instruction data, read in place: its bytes, and little-endian values at a byte offset. |
| `loadRaw` | `function loadRaw<T>(account: RemainingAccount \| AccountInfo): Account<T>` | A native (non-Anchor) program's own account as a fixed-layout struct, as a `#[repr(C)]` type's `load_checked` / `load_mut_checked` reads it: owned by this program (3007) and at least as large as the struct (3003). |
| `loadRawMut` | `function loadRawMut<T>(account: RemainingAccount \| AccountInfo): Mut<T>` | `loadRaw` for writing: also writable and loaded mutably once per instruction (2040). |
| `loadBorsh` | `function loadBorsh<T>(account: RemainingAccount \| AccountInfo): T` | A native program's Borsh account, as Rust's `try_from_slice_unchecked::<T>(&data)` reads it: the data from byte 0 decoded into a local `T` (a copy; write it back with `storeBorsh`). |
| `storeBorsh` | `function storeBorsh<T>(account: RemainingAccount \| Mut<AccountInfo>, value: T): void` | Write `value` into the account's data from byte 0 as Borsh, as Rust's `value.serialize(&mut *data)` does: only the encoded bytes are written (an Option that became None leaves the old bytes after it as they were); an account too small for the encoding fails with `ProgramError.BorshIoError`. |
| `BigVec` | `interface BigVec<T>` | A native program's zero-copy list over the rest of an account (SPL's `big_vec::BigVec`, the stake pool's validator list): a u32 length, then the elements back to back, in an account allocated up front. |
| `BigVecSlice` | `interface BigVecSlice<T>` | Some elements of a BigVec, in place: `bigVec.slice(start, end)`. |
| `loadRawAt` | `function loadRawAt<T>(account: RemainingAccount \| AccountInfo, offset: u64): Account<T>` | `loadRaw` / `loadRawMut` at a byte offset known only at run time (a native account whose parts start where its header says: Phoenix's market at byte 576). |
| `loadRawMutAt` | `function loadRawMutAt<T>(account: RemainingAccount \| AccountInfo, offset: u64): Mut<T>` | `loadRawAt` for writing: writable and claimed as `loadRawMut` is. |
| `rawArrayAt` | `function rawArrayAt<T>(account: RemainingAccount \| AccountInfo, offset: u64, capacity: u64): ReadonlyRawArray<T>` | A read-only view of `capacity` elements of `T` at `offset` in an account (see RawArray); `rawArrayMutAt` writes. |
| `rawArrayMutAt` | `function rawArrayMutAt<T>(account: RemainingAccount \| AccountInfo, offset: u64, capacity: u64): RawArray<T>` | `rawArrayAt` for writing: elements set in place (see RawArray). |
| `RawArray` | `interface RawArray<T>` | `capacity` elements of a fixed-size type packed in place from a run-time byte offset, the count known only at run time (a slab sized by its header). |
| `ReadonlyRawArray` | `interface ReadonlyRawArray<T>` | A RawArray of a read-only view (`rawArrayAt`): elements are read, not written. |
| `rbTreeAt` | `function rbTreeAt<K, V>(account: RemainingAccount \| AccountInfo, offset: u64, capacity: u64, compare?: (a: K, b: K) => bigint): ReadonlyRedBlackTree<K, V>` | lib-sokoban 0.3's RedBlackTree<K, V, capacity> at a run-time byte offset (see RedBlackTree): owned by this program (3007), its 32 + capacity × (16 + size(K) + size(V)) bytes within the data (ProgramError::AccountDataTooSmall), `rbTreeMutAt` writable and claimed as `loadRawMut` is. |
| `rbTreeMutAt` | `function rbTreeMutAt<K, V>(account: RemainingAccount \| AccountInfo, offset: u64, capacity: u64, compare?: (a: K, b: K) => bigint): RedBlackTree<K, V>` | `rbTreeAt` for writing: insert, remove and initialize with lib-sokoban's own writes (see RedBlackTree). |
| `RedBlackTree` | `interface RedBlackTree<K, V>` | lib-sokoban 0.3's `RedBlackTree<K, V, N>` in account data, byte for byte (Phoenix's order books and trader seats): at the offset, root u32, padding, the allocator (size u64, bump index u32, free list head u32), then `capacity` nodes of 16 register bytes + K + V, 1-based. |
| `ReadonlyRedBlackTree` | `interface ReadonlyRedBlackTree<K, V>` | A RedBlackTree of a read-only view (`rbTreeAt`): read, never changed. |
| `RbEntry` | `interface RbEntry<K, V>` | A node of a RedBlackTree: its key (read-only), its value (in place) and its index in the tree's node array (1-based). |
| `closeRaw` | `function closeRaw(account: RemainingAccount \| Mut<AccountInfo>, receiver: RemainingAccount \| Mut<AccountInfo>): void` | Close an account of this program as a native program does it by hand (Phoenix's Tombstone), in this order: `receiver.lamports += account.lamports`, `account.lamports = 0`, the owner set to the System Program, the data length set to 0 (`realloc(0, false)`: the bytes are not zeroed, the runtime drops them with the length). |
| `assignOwner` | `function assignOwner(account: RemainingAccount \| Mut<AccountInfo>, owner: Pubkey): void` | Set an account's owner in place (Rust's `AccountInfo::assign`). |
| `setReturnData` | `function setReturnData(bytes: IndexedList<u8>): void` | Set this instruction's return data to `bytes` as they are (Rust's `set_return_data(&bytes)`): a list of u8 such as a local `FixedVec<u8, N>`, a Vec or FixedVec in account data, or the instruction data or a slice of it. |
| `panic` | `function panic(message?: string \| null, location?: string): never` | Stop the program as a Rust `panic!` / `unwrap()` on `None` / `unreachable!()` does: the message is logged and the instruction fails with ProgramFailedToComplete (no error code). |
| `panicsAt` | `function panicsAt<T>(location: string, value: T): T` | `value`, with its checked arithmetic panicking as Rust's overflow checks do at `location` ("file:line:column", where the original's expression is): `panicsAt("src/quantities.rs:233:1", a + b)` logs "attempt to add with overflow" there (also "attempt to subtract / multiply with overflow", "attempt to divide by zero", "attempt to calculate the remainder with a divisor of zero", "attempt to negate with overflow", "attempt to divide with overflow", "attempt to shift left / right with overflow" for a shift amount past the width), as `panic` logs (see `PANIC_STYLE`), instead of failing with 5100 / 5101. |
| `abort` | `function abort(): never` | Stop the program as Rust's `abort` does on SBF (the allocator's out-of-memory error, `std::process::abort`): the runtime's `abort` syscall, which fails the instruction with ProgramFailedToComplete and logs "SBF program panicked" (no location, nothing else). |
| `logBase64` | `function logBase64(prefix: string, value: object): void` | Log `prefix` followed by the base64 (standard, padded) of a struct value's bytes, as a native program's `msg!("ray_log: {}", base64(bincode(log)))` does. |
| `logComputeUnits` | `function logComputeUnits(): void` | Log the compute units left (Rust's `sol_log_compute_units()`): the runtime writes "Program consumption: <N> units remaining", as the original's line, at the same place. |
